annotations.text: Topic filter (item 3): one “Topic” dropdown next to the search, ABOVE the table. The dropdown inside the expanded row goes away. With a filter active, the collapsed row shows the latest exchange MATCHING the filter (label “Latest question on topic Costs · date”). Funds without a matching exchange are hidden.

ISIN (item 4): the column shows the ISIN the latest question referred to, plus a chip “+4 classes”. All share classes, with the main tranche marked, are listed in the header of the expanded entry.

Version selector (item 7): hidden on the Inquiries tab – treated as a leftover.
Correction (item 8): two fields – “Corrected answer” (pre-filled) and “Correction note” (required, one sentence). Date and name are added by the system. Banner in the history = date + name + note.
Marker (item 9): speech-bubble icon after the fund name, the same marker on every share class. Click → Inquiries tab, search pre-filled with the fund, entry EXPANDED and highlighted.

VARIANT A · Minimal
Smallest distance from the current mockup: every open question is resolved in the simplest way, without changing the table structure.

Topic filter (item 3): chip bar with counters ABOVE the table. The filter narrows the list of funds, but the collapsed row always shows the fund’s latest exchange + badge “n matches for Costs”. When expanded, matches are highlighted, the rest dimmed, chronology kept.

ISIN (item 4): no ISIN column – the entry is per fund. The “Fund” cell shows “5 share classes” and the first ISIN; search still matches every ISIN/WKN. The “Documents” column returns as a separate column with a counter.

Version selector (item 7): replaced by the status “3 funds with inquiries · last updated …”.
Correction (item 8): one content field + optional reason. The previous version of the answer stays available to readers via “Show previous version”. The note is generated automatically.

Marker (item 9): chip “n inquiries” after the fund name. Click → Inquiries tab with the list filtered to the fund, entry COLLAPSED (the user expands it). Duplicate fund in the dialog: warning with a choice “Add to history” / “Open entry”.

VARIANT B · Fund level
Consistently “one fund = one history”: ISIN is removed as a column, share classes are shown as a property of the fund, the marker counts exchanges.

Topic filter (item 3): chip bar ABOVE the table + a dedicated “Topic” column in the row. The expanded entry groups the history by topic (chronological within a group), with topic navigation on the left and a “Show chronologically” switch. Topic becomes a required field when creating.

ISIN (item 4): the column shows the main tranche’s ISIN, labelled as such (“Main tranche LD”), plus “+4 more share classes”.

Version selector (item 7): stays for consistency with the other tabs, with an info icon “Inquiries are independent of versions”.

Correction (item 8): the analyst picks the type of correction (Typo / Factual correction / Addition) – the type controls the banner’s visibility; before/after is computed automatically from the text diff, the note is optional.

Marker (item 9): a dedicated narrow icon column at the start of the row, in the same place in all three tables. Click → side panel with the fund’s history without leaving the tab; link “Open in Inquiries tab”. Duplicates: already flagged in the fund picker.

VARIANT C · Topic-first
Topic as the axis: column, filter, grouped history and side panel. The biggest change; scales best for long, mixed histories.

SHARED FIXES – identical in all three variants
Items 1 and 2: the “Submitted by” and “FondsConsult analyst” fields are in dialogs A3/B3/C3. Item 5: new empty-state copy (separate for user and analyst). Item 6: “Save correction”, “Merkur Privatbank” in the navigation, two different placeholders, the real question in the Question field. Additionally: the sent confirmation (acceptance criterion) and the dialog for adding an exchange to an existing history (flow D).
The confirmation (G5) deliberately repeats that the entry does NOT change until FondsConsult publishes the answer – a requirement from the ticket (flow B, step 3).
Placeholders: “Request update” asks WHAT is out of date; “Ask follow-up question” asks WHAT is unclear. Two different intentions, one mechanism (email).
